Regulatory Transformation

Regulatory Transformation: navigating emerging risks, driving AI adoption and reducing regulatory burden

Regulators are facing a shifting operating environment as technology, markets, environmental pressures and societal expectations evolve faster than traditional regulatory frameworks. Fragmented data and limited intelligence continue to make risk prioritisation difficult.

There is a growing opportunity to use advanced analytics to better target regulatory effort. Many regulators are still working to integrate data across systems, uplift analytical capability and embed insights into everyday decision-making.

AI adoption is also becoming a core regulatory transformation issue. Regulators are seeking to balance opportunities for automation and improved risk identification with the need to manage governance, transparency, bias, legal risk, privacy and public confidence.

At the same time, governments are under pressure to reduce red tape, make faster decisions and manage fiscal constraints. This is driving interest in regulatory consolidation, shared-service models and more consistent approaches to regulatory delivery, while maintaining fairness and strong outcomes.

Regulation Hub Intelligence Brief

AI Brief 313 articles across 8 categories

The fortnight's dominant regulatory investment pattern consolidates across three vectors. First, the AER has simultaneously activated the EnergyConnect cost pass-through consultation, a draft ring-fencing exemption for AGN's hydrogen trials, and a revenue remake for the Waratah Super Battery — a concurrent network economics workload that signals a multi-year regulatory build cycle and live submission windows for network operator clients. Second, a Federal parliamentary inquiry into critical minerals, Geoscience Australia's precompetitive data investment, and Victoria's first antimony processing grant mark a government activation cycle across the critical minerals value chain where permitting, sovereign-capability, and supply-chain economics advisory mandates are forming now. Third, the McPhillamys Federal Court ruling has directly triggered a WA heritage laws overhaul, creating a national compliance gap for mining operators before new instruments are settled — KPMG's highest-urgency engagement window this fortnight. Across health, the TGA's completed AI digital scribe review delivers a government verdict on AI tools in clinical settings, opening a structured advisory lane for providers, while the Department of Health's landmark aged-care pay-equity package and NDIS 'future generations' framing signal imminent structural redesign mandates. AUSTRAC's live AML30 penalties and ASIC's digital asset law consultation (CP 392) create parallel regulated-entity pull across financial services clients. BD effort should be concentrated immediately on: heritage compliance rapid-assessment for mining clients, network regulatory design for AER-regulated networks, and responsible-AI advisory to health providers using the TGA verdict as the pitch anchor.

Cross-category themes

Regulators across every sector are simultaneously tightening enforcement and advancing structural reform, with ASIC, AUSTRAC, AHPRA, CASA, TEQSA, and WorkSafe Victoria all transitioning from guidance to active penalty action, creating urgent compliance uplift demand for clients who have been slow to embed new obligations. Overlapping reform cycles in AML/CTF, WHS, aged care, education standards, and defence supply chains, combined with cross-regulator attention to governance transparency and beneficial ownership, signal a sustained advisory market in gap analysis, board-level compliance positioning, and regulatory engagement strategy.

The NT regulatory landscape is active across three fronts. Tech & AI

Federal agencies are moving from AI policy to AI deployment at pace, with the AFP actively investing in detection technology targeting online harm and the Fair Work Commission issuing generative AI guidance prompts to contain an anticipated surge in unrepresented litigants — both signals that operational AI integration is outrunning governance frameworks. The TGA's completed digital scribe review marks Australia's first substantive regulatory adjudication of AI in a clinical workflow, opening immediate demand for implementation-pathway advice across the health and life sciences client base. CASA's continuation of broad-area BVLOS trials and the ACMA's spectrum coordination work on the 6 GHz band confirm that autonomous systems and next-generation connectivity infrastructure are live investment priorities, not pipeline. The federal AI Joint Select Committee is flagging sovereign capability and frontier model security access as headline concerns, which will translate into procurement and risk-framework mandates across Commonwealth agencies within this budget cycle. Deakin's $5 million ARC Training Centre for AI governance anchors a new research-to-regulation pipeline that KPMG should be visible in before it shapes the next wave of regulatory settings. Across these signals, the consistent gap is structured AI governance and assurance capability — the build-versus-buy and risk-tiering decisions that neither agencies nor ministers have the internal bench to make.

Capability reviews

Three signals this fortnight converge on a single theme: Australian government clients are confronting the gap between investment and actual delivered capability. The AFP is actively expanding its counter-foreign-interference function, which implies organisational redesign, workforce uplift, and new operational frameworks — precisely the terrain where capability maturity reviews land. Defence is the dominant story: ASPI's Canada comparison makes the case that Australia's forthcoming Defence Delivery Agency needs to be stress-tested against an integrated acquisition-and-industry-funding model before it is locked in, and KPMG should be shaping that conversation now, not after the DDA is legislated. The WA naval shipbuilding signal is starker still — ASPI is explicitly arguing that infrastructure spend without workforce capability, supply-chain depth, and industrial skills pipelines will fail, which is a direct brief for an independent capability review of the naval sustainment program. Across all three, the client pattern is national security and defence agencies investing at pace without the operating model rigour to sustain outcomes. KPMG's Defence & National Security and Workforce Transformation practices are the natural home for this work, and the DDA design window is the near-term forcing function.

Brief the AFP and TGA client partners this fortnight on KPMG's AI assurance and governance offering — both agencies have live deployments without a structured risk framework, and the Joint Select Committee's sovereign-capability findings will accelerate the mandate before the Mid-Year Economic and Fiscal Outlook. Brief the Defence & National Security partner this fortnight on positioning KPMG to lead an independent capability maturity review of the Defence Delivery Agency design — the Canada comparison ASPI has put into the public domain gives us a ready-made diagnostic frame, and the DDA architecture decision will close within 12 months. Brief the Health and Human Services sector partner this fortnight on a combined workforce-capability offer to the Department of Health, Disability and Ageing and AFSA, anchored to their active funding mandates, before both clients move to internal delivery models and close the advisory window. Brief the energy regulatory partner today on the four concurrent AER processes — EnergyConnect, AGN hydrogen, Transgrid, and Waratah Super Battery — and place KPMG's regulatory economics and revenue determination capability in front of network businesses before the Waratah remake decision closes the engagement window.

  • Tech & AI: Brief the AFP and TGA client partners this fortnight on KPMG's AI assurance and governance offering — both agencies have live deployments without a structured risk framework, and the Joint Select Committee's sovereign-capability findings will accelerate the mandate before the Mid-Year Economic and Fiscal Outlook.
  • Capability reviews: Brief the Defence & National Security partner this fortnight on positioning KPMG to lead an independent capability maturity review of the Defence Delivery Agency design — the Canada comparison ASPI has put into the public domain gives us a ready-made diagnostic frame, and the DDA architecture decision will close within 12 months.
  • Learning & development: Brief the Health and Human Services sector partner this fortnight on a combined workforce-capability offer to the Department of Health, Disability and Ageing and AFSA, anchored to their active funding mandates, before both clients move to internal delivery models and close the advisory window.
  • Risk & assurance: Brief the energy regulatory partner today on the four concurrent AER processes — EnergyConnect, AGN hydrogen, Transgrid, and Waratah Super Battery — and place KPMG's regulatory economics and revenue determination capability in front of network businesses before the Waratah remake decision closes the engagement window.

State-gov priorities

Cited strategic priorities across all 9 jurisdictions, refreshed bi-annually. Every source URL is .gov.au.

Housing supply is the single strongest cross-jurisdiction theme: every jurisdiction except NT carries a formal homes target (VIC 800,000 by 2034, QLD 1 million by 2046, NSW 170,000+ via TOD, ACT 30,000 by 2030, TAS 10,000 by 2032, SA $843M committed), and each couples that target with either density reform or social housing investment, creating sustained demand for planning-system assurance, program design, and delivery capability uplift. The clean-energy transition is equally pervasive but splits on mechanism: SA and TAS are chasing export-grade hydrogen and renewable generation surplus, NT and QLD are doubling down on extractive resources (QRIDP's 30-year mining vision, NT's defence-mining-agriculture pivot), while VIC, ACT, and CTH frame energy within broader net-zero and industrial-policy goals — a divergence that creates separate KPMG lanes in green-investment business cases versus resource-sector regulatory frameworks. Industrial policy has emerged as a coherent federal-state pattern: CTH's Future Made in Australia, WA's Made in WA, NSW's local manufacturing push, and SA's State Prosperity Project all target sovereign capability and supply-chain onshoring, and KPMG can offer economic-impact modelling, grant-program design, and industry-consultation facilitation across all four. Justice and community safety reform diverges sharply by political context: QLD's "adult crime, adult time" legislation and NT's crime reduction strategy reflect conservative law-and-order mandates, while NSW's DFV Safer Pathway and CTH's gender equality strategy reflect a social-investment framing — two distinct advisory postures are needed rather than a single national approach. Infrastructure strategy and long-term planning capability is a near-universal gap: ACT, SA, WA, and TAS all operate 20-year infrastructure strategies with periodic refresh cycles, and VIC's Plan to 2051 and NSW's TOD program require ongoing monitoring frameworks — KPMG's infrastructure advisory and program-assurance practice has a credible pipeline across every jurisdiction simultaneously. Finally, public-sector integrity and capability reform, led federally by the APS Reform Agenda and ACT's Parliamentary Agreement, signals appetite for organisational design, workforce strategy, and integrity-system reviews that can be packaged as a repeatable state-and-territory offering, particularly where incoming governments (QLD, NT) are restructuring agencies and redefining departmental mandates.

Last refreshed 2026-07-01. Bi-annual schedule; source URLs verified to .gov.au.

Commonwealth

  • Future Made in Australia
    The Treasury / Department of Industry, Science and Resources 2024-2034 (10-year, $22.7B package)
    Program design, sector assessment frameworks, investment mandate design, industry consultation, economic modelling, community benefit evaluation
    Source (2024-05-14)
  • Strengthening Medicare
    Department of Health, Disability and Ageing 2023-2027 (reform rolling); Budget 2025-26 expansion from Nov 2025
    Primary care reform evaluation, Urgent Care Clinic rollout support, workforce modelling, digital health implementation, Medicare integrity assurance
    Source (2024-05-14)
  • 2024 National Defence Strategy and Integrated Investment Program
    Department of Defence 2024-2034 ($330B Integrated Investment Program to 2033-34)
    Capability program assurance, workforce strategy, sovereign industrial capability priorities, AUKUS implementation support, capability reviews
    Source (2024-04-17)
  • APS Reform Agenda
    Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet / Australian Public Service Commission 2022-ongoing (4 pillars, 59 initiatives; Public Service Amendment Act 2024 enacted)
    Integrity and capability reviews, workforce strategy, stewardship framework design, data & digital workforce planning, contractor-to-APS conversion support
    Source (2024-12-01)
  • Working for Women: A Strategy for Gender Equality
    Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (Office for Women) 2024-2034 (10-year strategy)
    Gender impact analysis, workplace gender equality evaluation, Government Board appointment strategy support, pay-gap economic modelling, consultation design
    Source (2024-03-07)
  • Aged Care reform – transition to Support at Home
    Department of Health, Disability and Ageing Aged Care Act 2024 commenced 1 Nov 2025; CHSP transition to Support at Home by 1 Jul 2027
    Provider transition support, data and digital strategy implementation, workforce modelling, single assessment system evaluation, consumer journey design
    Source (2024-07-01)

New South Wales

  • Safe Staffing Levels in NSW public hospitals
    NSW Ministry of Health Phase one early 2024; full rollout 2,480 FTE nurses/midwives by June 2027
    Workforce modelling, implementation assurance, change management support, clinical governance advisory, rostering system review
    Source (2024-03-11)
  • Transport Oriented Development Program (TOD)
    Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure TOD planning controls commenced 13 May 2024; 15-year horizon; 170,000+ homes
    Precinct planning, inclusionary zoning advisory, infrastructure funding strategy, development feasibility, stakeholder consultation
    Source (2024-05-13)
  • Sydney Metro – Western Sydney Airport and Sydney Metro West
    Transport for NSW / Sydney Metro Western Sydney Airport line opens 2026; Metro West completion by 2032; network to 46 stations by 2030
    Program assurance, capability reviews, cost estimation reviews, land use integration, precinct economic analysis
    Source (2024-06-01)
  • Bringing back manufacturing to NSW (state-owned energy and rollingstock)
    Cabinet Office / Treasury NSW / Transport for NSW 2023-2027+ (current Parliament)
    Industrial strategy advisory, local content analysis, state-owned corporation establishment, procurement strategy, workforce development
    Source (2024-09-01)
  • NSW Budget 2025-26 priorities (essential services + diversified economy)
    NSW Treasury 2025-26 forward estimates to 2028-29
    Fiscal strategy advisory, expenditure review, program evaluation, revenue analysis, investment prioritisation
    Source (2025-06-24)
  • Safer Pathway – domestic and family violence response
    Department of Communities and Justice Statewide rollout ongoing; DFV reforms 2024-ongoing
    Service design, outcomes evaluation, risk assessment framework review, cross-agency data sharing advisory, program logic review
    Source (2024-01-01)

Victoria

  • Victoria's Housing Statement – The Decade Ahead 2024-2034
    Department of Transport and Planning 2024-2034 (800,000 homes / 80,000 per year target)
    Planning reform advisory, activity centre masterplans, affordable housing economics, surplus land unlocking, stakeholder consultation, LGA target negotiations
    Source (2023-09-20)
  • Plan for Victoria (long-term plan to 2051)
    Department of Transport and Planning Released Feb 2025; horizon to 2051 (2.24 million homes target)
    LGA housing target analysis, settlement pattern modelling, sustainability and climate policy integration, First Peoples self-determination in planning, infrastructure sequencing
    Source (2025-02-01)
  • Mental Health and Wellbeing reform (Royal Commission implementation)
    Department of Health 2021-2031 (decade of reform); Statewide Service and Capital Plan 2024-2037
    Service design, capital planning, workforce strategy, outcomes evaluation, lived experience engagement design, Mental Health Levy economic analysis
    Source (2024-07-01)
  • Treaty for Victoria / First Peoples' self-determination
    First Peoples – State Relations Statewide Treaty Bill 2025 introduced; negotiations ongoing
    Closing the Gap accountability framework design, service commissioning transition, policy impact analysis, governance advisory for new representative body
    Source (2025-02-01)
  • Breakthrough Victoria Fund – research and innovation commercialisation
    Department of Jobs, Skills, Industry and Regions 2020-2030 ($2B 10-year fund; $1.3B co-investment leveraged by 2024)
    Commercialisation strategy, innovation ecosystem review, investment thesis advisory, co-investment deal structuring, industry sector analysis
    Source (2024-06-30)

Queensland

  • Making Queensland Safer – adult crime, adult time youth justice reform
    Department of Youth Justice and Victim Support (renamed 1 Nov 2024) Making Queensland Safer Act 2024 assented 13 Dec 2024; Queensland Youth Justice Strategy 2024-2028
    Program logic review, early intervention evaluation, victim advocacy service design, circuit breaker sentencing assurance, regional reset program evaluation
    Source (2024-08-01)
  • Homes for Queenslanders housing plan
    Department of Housing and Public Works 2024-2046 (1 million new homes by 2046; 53,500 social homes)
    Housing target modelling, modular housing economics, social housing procurement, church/charity land strategy, planning reform advisory

  • A Fresh Start – cost-of-living and tax relief
    Queensland Treasury 100 Day Plan completed early 2025; ongoing measures 2024-2028

    Source (2025-02-01)
  • Queensland Resources Industry Development Plan (QRIDP)
    Department of Natural Resources and Mines, Manufacturing and Regional and Rural Development 2022-2052 (30-year vision; living document)
    Critical minerals strategy, decarbonisation roadmaps, regional community transition planning, ESG performance frameworks, royalty policy analysis

  • Bruce Highway Advisory Council and regional infrastructure
    Department of Transport and Main Roads Re-established 100 Day Plan period (late 2024); ongoing through current term
    Regional corridor prioritisation, cost-benefit analysis, safety-focused project business cases, stakeholder engagement with regional councils

  • Department of the Premier and Cabinet Strategic Plan 2024-2028
    Department of the Premier and Cabinet (Queensland) 2024-2028 (current through 30 April 2025 review; superseded by 2025-2029 plan)
    Central agency capability review, Cabinet support modernisation, policy quality uplift, intergovernmental strategy, corporate excellence frameworks
    Source (2024-06-28)

Western Australia

  • WA Government Priorities 2025-2029 (Jobs, Health, Housing, Community, Environment, Infrastructure and Services)
    Department of the Premier and Cabinet (WA) 2025-2029 (current parliamentary term)
    Cross-agency delivery coordination, outcomes-based budgeting advisory, capability reviews for new departments, program assurance

  • Made in WA Plan – $1B Strategic Industries Fund
    Department of Jobs, Tourism, Science and Innovation 2025-2035 ($500M additional investment; SIF total $1B over 10 years)

  • Defence West: WA Defence and Defence Industry Strategy 2025
    Department of Jobs, Tourism, Science and Innovation / Defence West 2025-2040 (15-year strategic vision)

  • Diversify WA: 2024 Update (economic development framework)
    Department of Jobs, Tourism, Science and Innovation Launched 2019; updated 2024; nine external-facing sectors

  • State Infrastructure Strategy (Infrastructure WA)
    Infrastructure WA 20-year strategy; IWA Annual Report and Government Response
    Infrastructure business case review, prioritisation methodology, capital program assurance, decarbonisation of infrastructure, asset recycling analysis
    Source (2024-01-01)

South Australia

  • State Prosperity Project
    Department of the Premier and Cabinet (SA) / Department for Energy and Mining Announced 2023; long-term (renewables, critical minerals, green manufacturing)

  • South Australia's Net Zero Strategy 2024-2030
